title: Panic Selling Continues; Trader Dumps Stocks Before Next 20% Drop | Chris Vermeulen
speaker: Chris Vermeulen (The Technical Traders)

macro_themes.view: The 10-year pullback is a technical 38-50% retracement; the longer-term trend in yields is still up and bonds are in a downtrend.
Money is flowing out of technology into equal-weight and defensive stocks; the Nasdaq trend has turned down.

macro_themes.theme: Precious metals in a bear market
macro_themes.view: Gold and silver are in stage-four declines and not assets to hold for growth, but are buys as insurance at measured-move levels.
The Middle East problem is here to stay; oil drifts higher until something breaks economically.
Expects at least a 20% real estate drop as rates rise and the economy softens, a big opportunity for buyers with cash in a couple of years.

calls.reason: Yields hit a Fibonacci measured-move target and pulled back to the 38.2% retracement; expects a bottom in the next sessions then higher, monthly chart points to a multi-month rally. Bond bounce is countertrend.
calls.quote: We should find yields put a bottom in over the next few sessions or the next week, and then they could go and head up to much higher pricing.

calls.condition: If QQQ closes below ~660 (50% retracement and pivot low), it could fall to ~555
calls.reason: Their Nasdaq strategy flipped to a downtrend; trailing stop hit two days earlier, closed QQQ/QLD longs to lock profits.
calls.quote: We are actually now have a negative trend a trend down for the Nasdaq, meaning you don't want to hold technology stocks at all right now.

calls.reason: S&P strategy still on a buy signal; broad market reaching a critical cycle low with yields peaking, so stocks should bounce.
calls.quote: We are still long the S&P 500... the S&P 500 is still in a buy signal
